newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down on late U.S. dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down on late U.S. dollar demand.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower against its U.S. counterpart on Monday on late U.S. dollar demand, likely from importers or state-run firms, dealers said.
The local unit ended at an intraday low of T$27.530 against Saturday's T$27.507 close. Turnover through dealers was a modest US$180 million.
"Late U.S. dollar demand likely from importers or state-run firms pushed down the Taiwan dollar," said one dealer.
The Taiwan dollar has been pressured recently by persistent foreign fund inflows to the bullish stock market.
"But on Monday, foreign funds seldom enter due to many overseas markets have not opened at the time when our market opens," the dealer said.
For Tuesday, a T$27.51-27.55 range was seen.
